---
title: "Textbooks"
---

### Required

This course makes use of several textbooks and other resources. I have attempted when possible to choose resources which are freely available.

1. Claus Wilke. [Fundamentals of Data Visualization](https://clauswilke.com/dataviz/)

This book is a comprehensive and highly readable guide to making visualizations that accurately reflect the data, tell a story, and look professional. It is freely available online and forms the backbone of the weekly readings.

2. Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic. *Storytelling with Data: A Data Visualization Guide for Business Professionals*

This book teaches the fundamentals of communicating effectively with data: choosing an appropriate visual, eliminating clutter, focusing attention, and building a narrative.

### Other Important Texts

1. Kieran Healy. [Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction](https://socviz.co/)

A hands-on introduction to making visualizations with `ggplot2` in R, freely available online.

2. William Cleveland. *The Elements of Graphing Data.* Hobart Press, 1994

A classic text on graphical perception theory from one of the pioneers of statistical graphics.

3. Rafe Donahue. [Fundamental Statistical Concepts in Presenting Data](https://biostat.app.vumc.org/wiki/pub/Main/RafeDonahue/fscipdpfcbg_currentversion.pdf)
